title: SYSK Selects: How Cockroaches Work
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the August episode "How Cockroaches Work," introduced by Chuck. The hosts discuss cockroach hygiene and disease risk, their survival history (about 300 million years, surviving the dinosaur extinction, nuclear war and winter speculation), body anatomy (head, thorax, abdomen, compound eyes, antennae, mouthparts, legs), fast movement, molting and limb regrowth, the head-off survival fact, breathing through spiracles, digestion with the crop and proventriculus, cerci sensing air flow, reproduction and ootheca types, social behavior and the robotic cockroach experiment (RoboRoach), and home prevention and control tips such as sealing cracks, bait traps, and natural repellents. The episode closes with a listener anecdote about a self-experiment with soap and water up the nose and in the eye.

segments.title: Selects intro and cockroach banter
segments.summary: Chuck introduces the Selects episode on cockroaches and the hosts joke about killing cockroaches, the song Lakukaracha, and The X Files.

segments.title: Cockroach hygiene and disease
segments.summary: The hosts say cockroaches are personally clean, groom their antennae and feet, and can spread bacteria and allergens through feces; a informal swab comparison with a man's hands is described.

segments.title: Species and how roaches spread to homes
segments.summary: Over 4,000 cockroach species exist, but mainly the German cockroach causes home infestations. The American, Oriental, brown-banded and Palmetto bug are also discussed, with transport via ships, planes and boxes.

segments.title: Survival history and extinction
segments.summary: Cockroaches have existed about 300 million years, outlasting dinosaurs. The hosts speculate about surviving nuclear war and say they likely would not survive nuclear winter, though they are more radiation resistant than most insects.

segments.title: Body structure, wings and molting
segments.summary: Describes the three body regions, downward-pointing heads, males with flight-capable wings, exoskeleton molting, bursicon hormone hardening the armor, and regrowing lost limbs.

segments.title: Head, brain, nervous system and breathing
segments.summary: Discusses the head, eyes, brain and ganglia, and the fact that a cockroach can live up to a week without its head, dying of thirst. Roaches breathe through spiracles in their sides.

segments.title: Eyes, antennae and mouthparts
segments.summary: Compound eyes give a mosaic view. Antennae sense pheromones and odors. Mouthparts include mandibles and maxillae for chewing.

segments.title: Legs, speed and movement
segments.summary: Three leg pairs (pro-, meso-, metathoracic) work together for walking; roaches move up to about three miles an hour in body-length terms, equivalent to very fast human speeds, and can cling to ceilings via their tarsi.

segments.title: Abdomen, circulation and fat body
segments.summary: The heart and hemocoel move blood without carrying oxygen, and the fat body stores energy.

segments.title: Digestion and cerci
segments.summary: Describes the crop, the toothy proventriculus that grinds wood and cellulose, the gastric caecum with enzymes and microbes, and cerci that sense air flow to dodge swats.

segments.title: Reproduction, oothecae and social behavior
segments.summary: Describes German and American cockroach reproductive rates, courtship with pheromones and wing flapping, ootheca egg cases, live birth in some species, parental care, and group roosting decisions. A robotic cockroach named InSpectre was used to lead roaches into the open.

segments.title: Home prevention and control
segments.summary: Advice on sealing cracks as small as 1.5 mm, using bait traps to track roaches, avoiding sprays and sound devices, keeping a clean house, and natural repellents like catnip oil, bay leaves and orange oil.

segments.title: Listener mail: soap and water self-experiment
segments.summary: A listener from Manchester, England, James, describes a self-experiment combining water up the nose with soap in the eye.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: The hosts ask for listener self-experiments and cockroach stories and point to social media and the website.
